body:
Found by #125's verify pass, on this board, 2026-08-28.

`hkb dispatch --loop 60` imports its modules once, at startup, and then ticks for hours. The global
`hkb` is a symlink into the checkout, so upgrading hkb — a merge to `main`, a `git pull`, an
`npm i -g` — changes the code on disk and changes nothing about the loop already running. Every
behaviour added since that process started is inert until a human notices and restarts it.

## Evidence

#137 (`69bf76a`, "Record a background worker's session from the tick") merged at 12:46. The loop that
launched attempt #125-1 at 13:02 had been running since **06:13**. Twenty minutes and twenty ticks
later, #125-1 still carried no `session_id` and no `transcript_path`, and neither did any of the 10
`protocol_violation`, 5 `timed_out` or 2 `crashed` rows #137 exists to stamp. Across all 89 attempts
on the board the only three with session fields are the three whose *worker* ran a terminal verb
after #135 merged — the `src/lifecycle.js` path, which runs in a fresh process every time.

So #137 is correct code that has never executed here, and nothing says so. `hkb doctor`'s new
`profile claude sessions` check (#134) reports `session recorded on 3/9 that filed a terminal verb`
— an ok line — because it asks whether *verbs* are stamping, which they are.

## Options

1. **The loop gives itself up.** Exit code 4 already means "the dispatcher loop gave itself up for a
   supervisor to restart", and `docs/wiki` and `README` already document a supervisor as the thing
   that restarts it. A tick that notices its own entry point has a newer mtime (or a different
   `packageVersion()`) than the one it loaded can exit 4 with `hkb: this loop is running <old>, the
   installed hkb is <new> — restarting`. Cheapest, and it self-heals on a supervised board.
2. **`hkb doctor` says it.** One line: the running loop's start time against the installed hkb's
   mtime. Honest, but the human still has to act.

(1) matches the existing ladder; (2) is a fallback for an unsupervised laptop loop. Either way the
rule is the same as #134's: a mechanism that cannot run should say so rather than read as ok.

## Done when

- A loop older than the hkb it would load either restarts itself or is reported.
- A board where the loop is current is unchanged, and pays nothing per tick for the check.
title: A dispatch --loop keeps the code it started with, so an upgrade never reaches it
